- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). input.description: Search for memo CRUD-related patterns in web/src
Find files with CRUD operations excluding proto definitions

content.text: Two key files stand out: `/bench/repo/web/src/hooks/useMemoQueries.ts` and `/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoEditor/services/memoService.ts`. Let me read those along with the connect.ts and action hooks.
Now let me read the connect.ts file to see the service client definition.
Now let me check the MemoActionMenu hooks and the reaction hooks for completeness.

Here is the complete research report.

---

## Primary Module: Memo CRUD Mutations and Queries

The main module containing memo CRUD mutations and queries is:

**`/bench/repo/web/src/hooks/useMemoQueries.ts`**

### Key Exports (with line numbers)

| Export | Type | Line |
|---|---|---|
| `memoKeys` | Query key factory object | 12 |
| `useMemos` | Query hook (list memos, non-paginated) | 112 |
| `useInfiniteMemos` | Infinite query hook (paginated list) | 122 |
| `useMemo` | Query hook (single memo by name) | 142 |
| `useLinkMetadata` | Query hook (link preview metadata) | 163 |
| `useCreateMemo` | Mutation hook (create) | 178 |
| `useUpdateMemo` | Mutation hook (update with field mask + optimistic updates) | 197 |
| `useDeleteMemo` | Mutation hook (delete) | 253 |
| `useMemoComments` | Query hook (list comments for a memo) | 272 |
| `useInfiniteMemoComments` | Infinite query hook (paginated comments) | 291 |

### Service Client

All hooks use `memoServiceClient`, imported at line 5:
```typescript
import { memoServiceClient } from "@/connect";
```

This client is defined in **`/bench/repo/web/src/connect.ts`** at line 197:
```typescript
export const memoServiceClient = createClient(MemoService, transport);
```

It is created from the generated `MemoService` descriptor imported at line 10:
```typescript
import { MemoService } from "./types/proto/api/v1/memo_service_pb";
```

The `transport` is a ConnectRPC transport (`@connectrpc/connect-web`) configured at line 184 with binary format and an auth interceptor.

---

## Secondary Module: MemoEditor Save Service

**`/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoEditor/services/memoService.ts`**

This is a higher-level service object (not a React hook) that orchestrates create/update with file uploads and field-mask diffing. It also uses `memoServiceClient` from `@/connect` (line 4). Its single public method `save()` is exported at line 76-123 and handles:
- Uploading local files (line 85)
- Updating an existing memo with a computed update mask (lines 89-101)
- Creating a new memo or comment (lines 104-122)

---

## Additional Related Files

- **`/bench/repo/web/src/hooks/useMemoShareQueries.ts`** -- Share-link CRUD hooks (`useMemoShares`, `useCreateMemoShare`, `useDeleteMemoShare`, `useSharedMemo`), also using `memoServiceClient`.

- **`/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoActionMenu/hooks.ts`** -- Consumer of `useUpdateMemo` and `useDeleteMemo` from `useMemoQueries.ts` (line 7). Provides higher-level action handlers (pin/unpin, archive/restore, copy link, check/uncheck tasks, delete).

- **`/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoView/hooks/useMemoActions.ts`** -- Thin wrapper around `useUpdateMemo` for unpin (line 1 imports from `useMemoQueries`).

- **`/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoReactionListView/hooks.ts`** -- Uses `memoServiceClient` directly (line 3) for reaction upsert/delete, and imports `memoKeys` from `useMemoQueries` for cache invalidation.

- **`/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoEditor/hooks/useLinkMemo.ts`** -- Uses `memoServiceClient` directly (line 3) for `listMemos` to search for memos to link as relations.

- **`/bench/repo/web/src/types/proto/api/v1/memo_service_pb.ts`** -- The generated protobuf/ConnectRPC service definition and message schemas.
